title: Mass number, atomic number and isotopes

notes.definition: The atomic number is the number of protons in an atom, and the mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons. Isotopes are atoms of the same element (same number of protons) with different numbers of neutrons.
explanation: In an atom, the number of electrons is equal to the number of protons in the nucleus. Each proton has a positive charge and each electron has an equal negative charge, so the charges cancel. This is why atoms have no overall electrical charge.

The number of protons in an atom is called its atomic number (symbol Z). Every atom of a particular element has the same number of protons, so the atomic number identifies the element. All carbon atoms have 6 protons and all sodium atoms have 11. If the number of protons changed, the atom would become a different element.

The total number of protons and neutrons in an atom is called its mass number (symbol A). To find the number of neutrons, subtract the atomic number from the mass number: neutrons = A − Z. Atoms are written in symbol notation with the mass number at the top left and the atomic number at the bottom left of the chemical symbol, for example ²³₁₁Na. This sodium atom has 11 protons, 11 electrons and 23 − 11 = 12 neutrons.

Atoms of the same element can have different numbers of neutrons. These atoms are called isotopes of that element. Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers. For example, carbon-12 (¹²₆C) has 6 neutrons and carbon-14 (¹⁴₆C) has 8 neutrons. The number after the name is the mass number. Some isotopes are stable and others are unstable (radioactive).

Atoms can lose electrons. If an atom loses one or more of its outer electrons it has more protons than electrons, so it becomes a positive ion. Losing one electron gives a charge of +1, losing two gives +2, and so on. The nucleus does not change, so it is still the same element.
keyFacts: In an atom, number of electrons = number of protons, so atoms have no overall charge.
All atoms of the same element have the same number of protons.
Mass number = number of protons + number of neutrons.
Number of neutrons = mass number − atomic number.
In symbol notation, mass number is written at the top and atomic number at the bottom, e.g. ²³₁₁Na.
Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.
Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
An atom that loses one or more outer electrons becomes a positive ion.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think isotopes are different elements because they have different masses.
misconceptions.right: In fact isotopes are the same element, because they have the same number of protons. Only the number of neutrons is different.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the mass number is the number of neutrons.
misconceptions.right: In fact the mass number is protons plus neutrons. Subtract the atomic number to get the neutrons.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think an atom becomes positive by gaining protons.
misconceptions.right: In fact the nucleus does not change. An atom becomes a positive ion by losing one or more outer electrons.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the bigger number in nuclide notation is always the atomic number.
misconceptions.right: In fact the bigger number (at the top) is the mass number; the smaller number (at the bottom) is the atomic number.

realWorld: Carbon-14, a radioactive isotope of carbon, is used to date ancient wood, bone and cloth.
Nuclear power stations use uranium-235, an isotope that makes up less than 1% of natural uranium, so the fuel has to be enriched.
Hydrogen-2 (deuterium) and hydrogen-3 (tritium) are isotopes that can be used as fuel in experimental fusion reactors.
examTips: Always find neutrons by subtracting: mass number − atomic number. Write the subtraction down to secure the method mark.
In a definition of isotopes, mention both the same number of protons AND a different number of neutrons.
Electrons only equal protons in a neutral atom. For an ion, adjust the number of electrons to match the charge.
Learn the layout of nuclide notation: mass number on top, atomic number below.
summary: Atoms are neutral because electrons = protons.
Atomic number = protons; it identifies the element.
Mass number = protons + neutrons; neutrons = A − Z.
Isotopes: same protons, different neutrons, different mass numbers.
Losing outer electrons turns an atom into a positive ion.

questions.question: What does the atomic number of an atom tell you?
options: The number of protons plus neutrons
markScheme: 1 mark: The number of protons
questions.explanation: Atomic number is the number of protons. Protons plus neutrons is the mass number.

questions.question: What is the mass number of an atom?
options: The number of protons plus neutrons
The number of protons plus electrons
The mass of the atom in grams
markScheme: 1 mark: The number of protons plus neutrons
questions.explanation: Mass number is the total of protons and neutrons in the nucleus. Electrons have very little mass and are not counted.

questions.question: Why does an atom have no overall charge?
options: It has equal numbers of protons and neutrons
Neutrons cancel the charge of the protons
It has equal numbers of protons and electrons
markScheme: 1 mark: It has equal numbers of protons and electrons
questions.explanation: Each proton (+) is balanced by an electron (−). Neutrons have no charge so cannot cancel anything.

questions.question: Which pair of atoms are isotopes of the same element?
markScheme: 1 mark: ¹²₆C and ¹⁴₆C
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number (bottom number) but different mass numbers. Both carbon atoms have Z = 6. ¹⁴₆C and ¹⁴₇N have the same mass number but are different elements.

questions.question: How many neutrons are in an atom of ²⁷₁₃Al?
markScheme: 1 mark: 14
questions.explanation: Neutrons = 27 − 13 = 14. 13 is the number of protons and 40 comes from adding instead of subtracting.

questions.question: An atom loses one outer electron. What does it become?
markScheme: 1 mark: A positive ion
questions.explanation: Losing a negative electron leaves more protons than electrons, so the atom becomes a positive ion. The nucleus is unchanged, so it is the same element.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the nuclei of two isotopes of helium.
Which statement about the two isotopes is correct?
options: They have different numbers of protons
They have the same mass number
They have different numbers of neutrons
They have different numbers of electrons in the neutral atom
markScheme: 1 mark: They have different numbers of neutrons
questions.explanation: Isotopes differ only in the number of neutrons. Neutral atoms of both isotopes have the same numbers of protons and electrons.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the numbers of particles in an atom of potassium (K).
Which is the correct symbol for this atom?
markScheme: 1 mark: ³⁹₁₉K
questions.explanation: Mass number = 19 + 20 = 39 goes on top, and atomic number = 19 goes at the bottom. The mass number is always the larger number.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the numbers of protons and neutrons in three atoms, X, Y and Z.
Which statement is correct?
options: Y and Z are the same element
All three are isotopes of one element
markScheme: 1 mark: X and Y are isotopes
questions.explanation: Only X and Y have the same number of protons (26), so they are the same element with different neutron numbers: isotopes. Z has 27 protons, so it is a different element.

questions.question:
An atom of fluorine is represented as ¹⁹₉F
Determine the number of neutrons in this atom.
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 19 − 9 = 10.

questions.question:
Uranium has an atomic number of 92.
Determine the number of neutrons in an atom of uranium-238.
questions.explanation: The 238 is the mass number. 238 − 92 = 146 neutrons.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows information about two isotopes of chlorine.
Calculate the number of neutrons in an atom of chlorine-37.
markScheme: 1 mark: 20
questions.explanation: Chlorine-37 has mass number 37. 37 − 17 = 20 neutrons. Chlorine-35 has 18 neutrons.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the numbers of protons and neutrons in an iron atom.
The iron atom loses 3 outer electrons to form an ion.
Calculate the number of electrons in the ion.
markScheme: 1 mark: neutral atom has 26 electrons
questions.explanation: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons (26). Losing 3 leaves 23. The neutrons are irrelevant here.

questions.question:
Isotope P of lead has an atomic number of 82 and a mass number of 208.
Isotope Q of lead has 4 fewer neutrons than isotope P.
Calculate the mass number of isotope Q.
markScheme: 1 mark: neutrons in P = 208 − 82 = 126, so Q has 122
1 mark: mass number of Q = 82 + 122 = 204
questions.explanation: Isotope Q has the same 82 protons but 122 neutrons, so its mass number is 204. Shortcut: 4 fewer neutrons means mass number 4 smaller.

questions.question: Define the term isotopes.
markScheme: 1 mark: atoms of the same element / same number of protons
1 mark: with different numbers of neutrons
questions.explanation: Both parts are needed: same protons and different neutrons.

questions.question: State what is meant by the mass number of an atom.
acceptedAnswers: total number of protons and neutrons
markScheme: 1 mark: total number of protons and neutrons (in the nucleus)
questions.explanation: Mass number counts all particles in the nucleus.

questions.question:
An atom is written as ⁵⁶₂₆Fe.
State the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in this atom.
markScheme: 1 mark: 26 protons
1 mark: 30 neutrons
1 mark: 26 electrons
questions.explanation: Protons = atomic number = 26. Neutrons = 56 − 26 = 30. The atom is neutral, so electrons = 26.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the nuclei of carbon-12 and carbon-14.
Explain why carbon-12 and carbon-14 are the same element.
markScheme: 1 mark: they have the same number of protons (6) / same atomic number
1 mark: the number of protons determines the element
questions.explanation: The element depends only on the number of protons. The different number of neutrons changes the mass, not the element.

questions.question: A sodium atom loses one electron. Explain why the particle formed has a charge of +1.
markScheme: 1 mark: it now has one more proton than electrons (11 protons, 10 electrons)
1 mark: so one positive charge is not cancelled, giving +1
questions.explanation: In the atom, 11 positive charges balance 11 negative charges. After losing an electron, one positive charge is left unbalanced.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows information about two atoms, A and B.
A student says that A and B are isotopes because they have the same mass number.
Explain why the student is wrong.
markScheme: 1 mark: A and B have different atomic numbers / numbers of protons
1 mark: so they are different elements, and isotopes must be the same element
questions.explanation: Isotopes must share an atomic number. Having the same mass number is irrelevant.

questions.question: State where the mass number is written in nuclide notation such as ²³₁₁Na.
markScheme: 1 mark: at the top (left) of the symbol
questions.explanation: Mass number at the top, atomic number at the bottom.

questions.question: Describe how the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons in a neutral atom of ³⁵₁₇Cl compare with those in a neutral atom of ³⁷₁₇Cl.
markScheme: 1 mark: both have 17 protons
1 mark: both have 17 electrons
1 mark: chlorine-35 has 18 neutrons and chlorine-37 has 20 neutrons (2 more)
questions.explanation: Isotopes share proton and electron numbers in neutral atoms. Only the neutron number differs: 35 − 17 = 18 and 37 − 17 = 20.

questions.question: Which change to an atom would make it into a different element?
markScheme: 1 mark: Gaining a proton
questions.explanation: The element depends on the number of protons. Changing neutrons gives a different isotope, and losing electrons gives an ion of the same element.

questions.question: In the name carbon-14, what does the number 14 represent?
markScheme: 1 mark: The mass number
questions.explanation: The number in an isotope name is the mass number (protons + neutrons). Carbon-14 has 6 protons and 8 neutrons.

questions.question: Compare the atoms ¹⁶₈O and ¹⁸₈O. Use the terms atomic number, mass number and isotope in your answer.
markScheme: Indicative content: both have atomic number 8, so 8 protons; both are oxygen; both neutral atoms have 8 electrons; mass numbers 16 and 18; neutrons 8 and 10; same element with different numbers of neutrons, so they are isotopes; ¹⁸O has greater mass.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): clear comparison of protons, neutrons and electrons with correct numbers and correct use of all three terms.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): some correct numbers or terms with little comparison.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: A good comparison gives similarities and differences with numbers: same protons and electrons, different neutrons, so isotopes.

questions.question:
An element has two isotopes: ⁶³₂₉Cu and ⁶⁵₂₉Cu.
Explain what the numbers in the symbols tell you, explain why the atoms are isotopes, and describe what happens to the atom and its charge when ⁶³₂₉Cu loses two outer electrons.
markScheme: Indicative content: 29 is the atomic number: 29 protons in both; 63 and 65 are mass numbers: protons + neutrons; neutrons 34 and 36; same number of protons so same element; different neutrons so isotopes; neutral atoms have 29 electrons because electrons = protons; losing two outer electrons leaves 27 electrons; 29 protons and 27 electrons gives a charge of +2; it becomes a positive ion; nucleus unchanged so still copper with mass number 63.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): all three parts explained with correct numbers and clear reasoning.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): two parts explained correctly, or all three with some errors.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): basic statements, e.g. identifies atomic number or mass number, with little explanation.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Work through each part with numbers: 63 − 29 = 34, 65 − 29 = 36, and 29 − 27 = +2 for the ion.
